newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to borrow $4.1 bln external debt in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to borrow $4.1 bln external debt in 1997.

text.p: Thailand plans to borrow $4.1 billion abroad in fiscal 1997 to finance major infrastructure projects, acting Finance Minister Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi said on Friday.

Those projects include the construction of a second Bangkok international airport, an underground mass transit system, an expressway and the purchase of new aircrafts by Thai Airways International Plc, Chaiyawat told reporters.
The plan will go to the cabinet for final approval early next month, he said.
In fiscal 1996 ending September 30, 1996, the Thai government borrowed a total of $3.7 billion abroad, he said. The fiscal year begins on October 1.
He said the government's planned overseas borrowing in 1997 will still be in line with the finance ministry's strict monetary policy.

"This year's overseas borrowing will still comply with the finance ministry's policy of keeping foreign debt at an appropriate level. It's only $400 million higher than 1996's borrowing abroad," Chaiyawat said.
Somchai Richupan, director general of the Fiscal Policy Office, said the government's foreign borrowing of $4.1 billion in 1997 would not have an adverse impact on the economy.
"The rise in foreign borrowing this year will have no impact on the economy because Thailand has high capability to repay foreign debt," Somchai said.
